q: The general solution of cos θ = 0 is (n ∈ Z):
x: cos θ = 0 at π/2 and 3π/2 in one turn, which are π apart, so θ = π/2 + nπ. θ = π/2 + 2nπ misses 3π/2, and θ = nπ solves sin θ = 0.

q: The general solution of cos θ = 1/√2 is (n ∈ Z):
x: The principal value is π/4 and cos is even with period 2π, so θ = 2nπ ± π/4. θ = nπ ± π/4 would also include 3π/4, where cos θ = −1/√2.

q: The general solution of cot θ = −1 is (n ∈ Z):
x: cot θ = −1 means tan θ = −1, whose principal solution is −π/4, and tan has period π, so θ = nπ − π/4 (this includes 3π/4 and 7π/4). The 2nπ forms each keep only one of these two families.

q: The solutions of sin 3θ = −1 in the interval 0 ≤ θ < 2π are:
x: 3θ = 3π/2 + 2nπ, so θ = π/2 + 2nπ/3, giving π/2, 7π/6, 11π/6 in [0, 2π). Check 7π/6: sin(7π/2) = −1. The set π/6, 5π/6, 3π/2 solves sin 3θ = +1.

q: How many solutions does cos θ = −0.3 have in the interval 0 ≤ θ < 2π?
x: Since −1 < −0.3 < 1, the line y = −0.3 cuts one full wave of y = cos θ twice: once in the second quadrant and once in the third, where cosine is negative.

q: The general solution of sin 2θ = 1 is (n ∈ Z):
x: 2θ = π/2 + 2nπ, so θ = π/4 + nπ after dividing everything, including the period, by 2. Check θ = 5π/4: sin(5π/2) = 1.

q: The general solution of sin θ = −1/√2 is (n ∈ Z):
x: The principal value is −π/4, so θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(−π/4) = nπ − (−1)ⁿ π/4: n = 0 gives −π/4, n = 1 gives 5π/4, both with sine −1/√2. θ = nπ − π/4 wrongly includes 3π/4.

q: The general solution of the pair of equations sin θ = −1/2 and tan θ = 1/√3, holding together, is (n ∈ Z):
x: In one turn sin θ = −1/2 at 7π/6 and 11π/6, and tan θ = 1/√3 at π/6 and 7π/6; only 7π/6 is common. Repeating every 2π gives θ = 2nπ + 7π/6; the form nπ + π/6 also includes π/6, where sin θ = +1/2.

q: The solutions of sin θ cos θ = 1/4 in the interval 0 ≤ θ < π are:
x: sin θ cos θ = ½ sin 2θ, so sin 2θ = 1/2 with 0 ≤ 2θ < 2π, giving 2θ = π/6 or 5π/6, so θ = π/12 or 5π/12. The pair π/6, 5π/6 solves sin θ = 1/2 instead.

q: How many solutions does sin θ + sin 3θ = 0 have in the interval 0 ≤ θ ≤ π?
x: sin 3θ + sin θ = 2 sin 2θ cos θ = 0. sin 2θ = 0 gives θ = 0, π/2, π and cos θ = 0 gives π/2 again, so the distinct solutions are 0, π/2, π. Counting π/2 twice gives 4.

q: The solutions of sec θ + tan θ = √3 in the interval 0 ≤ θ < 2π are:
x: Multiply by cos θ: 1 + sin θ = √3 cos θ, so √3 cos θ − sin θ = 1, i.e. 2 cos(θ + π/6) = 1, giving θ = π/6 or 3π/2. At 3π/2, cos θ = 0 and sec θ, tan θ are undefined, so reject it. Check π/6: 2/√3 + 1/√3 = √3.

q: The solutions of 4 cos³θ − 3 cos θ = 0 in the interval 0 ≤ θ ≤ π are:
x: Factor: cos θ(4 cos²θ − 3) = 0, so cos θ = 0 (θ = π/2) or cos θ = ±√3/2 (θ = π/6, 5π/6). The left side is cos 3θ, and cos 3θ = 0 gives the same three angles. Dividing by cos θ loses π/2.

q: The general solution of cos 2θ = cos²θ is (n ∈ Z):
x: Write cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1: then cos²θ = 1, so cos θ = ±1 and θ = nπ. Check with cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ: the equation becomes sin²θ = 0, again θ = nπ. θ = 2nπ keeps only cos θ = 1.

q: The general solution of sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2 is (n ∈ Z):
x: sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = −cos 2θ, so cos 2θ = −1/2, 2θ = 2nπ ± 2π/3, θ = nπ ± π/3. Check π/3: 9/16 − 1/16 = 1/2. Missing the minus sign gives cos 2θ = 1/2 and nπ ± π/6.

q: The general solution of 2 cos²θ + 5 sin θ − 4 = 0 is (n ∈ Z):
x: Replace cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ: 2 sin²θ − 5 sin θ + 2 = 0, i.e. (2 sin θ − 1)(sin θ − 2) = 0. sin θ = 2 is impossible, so sin θ = 1/2 and θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ π/6. Check π/6: 2(3/4) + 5/2 − 4 = 0.

q: The solutions of 2 sin θ tan θ = 3 in the interval 0 ≤ θ < 2π are:
x: 2 sin²θ/cos θ = 3 gives 2(1 − cos²θ) = 3 cos θ, i.e. 2cos²θ + 3cos θ − 2 = 0, (2cos θ − 1)(cos θ + 2) = 0, so cos θ = 1/2: θ = π/3, 5π/3. Check 5π/3: 2(−√3/2)(−√3) = 3.
